articleTitle: Sliding-Mode-Based Driving Torque Distribution for Dynamic Control of Dual-Motor Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper presents an anti-slip control system for dual-motor electric vehicles, utilizing a sliding mode control (SMC) approach. The control strategy calculates the torque distribution coefficients for the front and rear motors to mitigate slip and enhance vehicle stability. By applying the sliding mode method, the controller ensures robust performance under varying road conditions, reducing the risk of loss of traction. The proposed system is tested by simulations with representative scenarios to validate its effectiveness in maintaining low slip ratios and improving the overall performance of the vehicle, especially in low-friction environments.

articleTitle: Development of Wide-Angle Fovea Lens Taking Into Account Rapid Camera Work
abstract: Wide-Angle Fovea sensor (WAF sensor) is a well-known visual sensor in the field of robot vision with unique specifications biologically-inspired from the primate visual system. Resolution of its input image is the highest at the center of its field of view (FOV), and rapidly decreases toward the peripheral FOV. The type of WAF sensor realized using a special-made wide-angle lens simultaneously achieves the following two contradictory characteristics: (1) wide FOV and (2) high resolution (although this is partially achieved only in the central FOV). In addition, the WAF sensor requires eye movement similar to the human eye, and is used in combination with a camera work device. The high-definition WAF lens we prototyped previously had a sufficiently high optical performance, but it had a weak point that its first lens surface on the object side could not be protected by the lens barrel or protective cover glass during camera work because of too much protrusion of the first lens. In this paper, we propose a high-definition wide-angle fovea lens that is designed to avoid damage to the first lens during high-speed camera work. In order to solve the above problems, we design and manufacture a prototype with the following two points as design goals. (1) It has the same target specification as the previous WAF lens. (2) In order to greatly reduce the protrusion of the first lens, in addition to the four surfaces in the front lens group used in the previous prototype, another aspheric surface is added to the rear lens group. In the prototype, we succeeded in significantly reducing the protrusion of the first lens from 10.4mm to 2.2mm. To evaluate its performance, we conducted imaging experiments and optical resolution inspection using MTF measurements, and discussed the results.

Index Terms: Center Of The Field Of View

articleTitle: Modeling of Airflow Disturbance Force and Feedforward Controller Design in Pneumatic Valves
abstract: Pneumatic valves are vital components for controlling flow rates in general industrial applications. To control the flow rate of a valve precisely, this study focuses on controlling the valve body position, primarily determining the flow rate. Fast and precise control of the valve body position requires suppressing disturbance forces caused by air pressure dynamics. The authors address this issue with a feedforward control method by modeling the airflow disturbance force, which is estimated from feedforward inputs obtained through iterative learning control. The developed approach compensates for the airflow disturbance force under various target trajectories and pressure differences. The valve body position and flow rate tracking experiments validate the performance improvements in terms of settling time and overshoot.

articleTitle: A Novel Quadruple Dispensing Heads Sticking Adhesive Tape Robot System and Its Applications
abstract: Industrial robots are increasingly being used to assist and replace workers in factories to address the global labor shortage in various applications. The use of robots can provide many benefits to the effective production and manufacturing. Taping is one of the robots' applications. However, current tape robots can only tape one strip at a time, which can be time-consuming in practice if multiple strips of tape are required at the same time for special workpieces. This paper presents a novel sticking adhesive tape robot system. As the object to be taped are four-line hot pipes to be attached on the outer shell of refrigerator, thus four strips of tape are required at the same time before assembly process. The proposed robot system contains the novel tooling called “Quadruple Dispensing Heads”. This tooling was developed to tape four strips of tape to be applied simultaneously. This tooling can adjust the gap of tape strips from 80mm to 110mm. Moreover, the research objective is to produce a robot system that can apply tape with higher quality and faster than human workers, so that human workers can move on to more complicated tasks instead of performing repetitive, routine tasks that do not require such special skills and knowledge. As the result, our proposed system can achieve the four lines of I.Sm length, through IS7N pushing force (when operate the air working pressure at O.SMPa) sticking taping task perfectly with 100% success rate of experiments in just 3 seconds and faster than human worker significantly. Since, human worker needs about 3 seconds per each I.5m taping line. Therefore, human needs approximately 12 seconds in total for four lines. Accordingly, our proposed robot system is faster than human worker in four times.

articleTitle: Thermal-to-Color Image Translation Using Heat Conduction for 3D Mapping in Low-Visibility Environments
abstract: For safe firefighting and rescue operations at the scene of a fire, it is extremely important to accurately assess the situation inside a building. Currently, however, it is very difficult to generate a three-dimensional map in an environment filled with smoke and dust. To solve this problem, this study attempts to generate a three-dimensional map using a thermal camera, which is less susceptible to smoke. The thermal image acquired by a thermal camera is a grayscale image based on temperature gradients, which limits the number of feature points that can be obtained. In particular, it is difficult to extract feature points in environments where there is little temperature variation, making map generation difficult. In order to enable effective map generation even in such environments, this research aims to improve map generation accuracy by converting thermal images from thermal cameras into RGB images using deep learning.

articleTitle: A High Performance Disturbance Observer
abstract: This paper proposes a novel Disturbance Observer (DOb), termed the High-Performance Disturbance Observer (HPDOb), which achieves more accurate disturbance estimation compared to the conventional DOb, thereby delivering significant improvements in robustness and performance for motion control systems. The conventional and proposed DObs are analysed and synthesised in the discrete-time domain to fully capture their dynamic behaviours in real-world applications. This allows us to adjust the stability and performance of DOb-based digital robust motion control systems more effectively in practice. The conventional DOb is synthesised by assuming that the internal and external disturbances of a servo system does not change within the sampling period. Despite its simplicity, the constant disturbance model is impractical in many motion control applications. To address this issue, a more realistic disturbance model is utilised in the synthesis of the HPDOb, which is carried out in two steps. In the first step, a predictor is employed to estimate the disturbance change within the sampling period. The predictor can be implemented using the conventional DOb. In the second step, the predicted disturbance change is substituted into the high performance observer's dynamic model so that disturbances are estimated more accurately. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed HPDOb significantly enhances the accuracy of disturbance estimation. This approach benefits a wide range of motion control applications by providing more accurate disturbance estimates to motion controllers, thereby enhancing both the robustness and performance of position control and sensorless force control systems.

articleTitle: Thrust Control with Switching in Electrodynamic Propulsion Systems with Corona Discharge
abstract: Electroaerodynamics (EAD) is one phenomenon that manipulates gas with high voltage. Corona discharge is a typical example and is known to produce thrust quietly without moving parts. Therefore, it is expected to be utilized in various ways, such as a thrust source of drones. As thrust with corona discharge depends on the applied voltage, it is necessary to manipulate the applied voltage for thrust control. However, large-scale systems require several tens of kV, and there is little adequate research on these systems. Thus, an adequate switching method is essential, and it is also crucial to elucidate the effect of switching on thrust. Hence, this study conducted thrust control with corona discharge and analyzed the influence of switching on thrust. Specifically, a resistor is connected in series to the electrode, and a switching element is connected in parallel with the resistor. The proposed method stabilizes and limits the voltage applied to the switching element and effectively controls the thrust and the voltage applied to the electrode. Two experiments were conducted to reveal the electrical characteristics of the electrode in corona discharge and confirm the effectiveness of the proposal. The first experiment showed the potential of switching for the electrode with corona discharge on the collector side. Moreover, the second experiment demonstrated that the proposed switching method worked properly, and thrust can be controlled by changing the duty ratio of switching. The achievements of this study are expected to control levitation systems EAD, such as corona discharge, and realize stable control.

articleTitle: Vibration Suppression and Disturbance Rejection Based on Equivalent Mass and Stiffness Matrices
abstract: This paper proposes vibration suppression and disturbance rejection methods for multi-degrees-of-freedom (MDOF) manipulators with flexible joints in the workspace. The proposed methods utilize an equivalent mass matrix (EMM) and equivalent stiffness matrix (ESM) that represent the mass and stiffness in the workspace, respectively. In conventional methods, variations of EMM and ESM can degrade vibration suppression and disturbance rejection performances. Therefore, the proposed methods employ a workspace observer (WOB), resonance ratio control, and load-side workspace observer (LWOB). The WOB and resonance ratio control fix the EMM to constant values and realize stable vibration suppression. The LWOB improves ro-bustness by compensating for disturbances. The stability analyses reveal the parameter conditions. The simulation results show that the proposed methods suppress vibrations and disturbances in the workspace.

articleTitle: Positioning Control for Voice Coil Motor Using Unbalanced Multilevel Inverter Topology
abstract: This article proposes a new multi-level inverter (MLI) based on flying capacitor inverter (FCI), with focused on high-precision positioning control for a voice coil motor (VCM). Multi-level inverters (MLIs) have the characteristic that increasing the number of output voltage levels reduces the output voltage error. However, as the number of levels increases, the number of circuit elements increases, and the circuit becomes more complex. In addition, the output voltage amplitude for each level is constant in conventional inverters. As a result, such as high-precision positioning control of VCM, designing an appropriate inverter for a reference wave that contains a large amount of low-voltage components increases the number of circuit elements. Therefore, this paper proposes a MLI with two unbalanced dc-input voltages, referred to as unbalanced MLIs (UMLIs) hereinafter. This topology uses two different dc-input voltages, and it is possible to reduce the output voltage level in extremely low-voltage range compared to other voltage levels. Simulation results when the high-precision positioning control of the VCM confirm that the proposed UMLIs improves the control performance compared to the conventional FCIs with equal number of output voltage levels and uniform level widths.

articleTitle: A PID-backstepping Hybrid Position and Attitude Control of a Bi-copter AUV with a Moving Mass
abstract: This research aims to design a bi-copter AUV and evaluate its feasibility. Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) that sail independently without cables and human operators are in the spotlight as an alternative to human divers. To miniaturize AUVs to operate in narrow spaces, we propose an AUV with two thrusters and two pitch angle servo motors: a “bi-copter” AUV. The bi-copter is expected to be power efficient, and have high turning performance. However, precise and robust control performance is required to overcome its underactuated characteristics and disturbances. To enhance pitch motion stability, a Pitch Motion Compensator (PMC) with a Pitch Angle Disturbance Observer (PADO) is implemented and controls the position of a moving mass inside the AUV body. We propose a PID-Backstepping Hybrid (PBH) control composed of the PID position controller and the backstepping attitude (roll and yaw motion) controller for the position and attitude control. In addition, We propose the yaw angle reference value calculation methodology to control the y position indirectly. Our proposed method is evaluated by the simulations using MATLAB/Simulink and Simscape including wave disturbance and its feasibility is confirmed.

articleTitle: On Analysis of Applying Iterative Learning Control to a Closed-Loop Three-Phase Linear Stepper-Motor
abstract: Interposers, crucial for connecting multiple chips, e.g., CPUs and memory, are expected to play a critical role for further improving the performance of integrated circuits. Seeking cost-effective and high-speed/high - precision manufacturing of next-generation interposers, this study aims to apply iterative learning control to a prototype three-phase linear stepper-motor. Experimental validation confirms desirable tracking performance to a noise-level-error by applying iterative learning control to the constructed closed-loop system.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Position of Loaded Packages in a Roll Cage Cart: Estimating the Placement Layout of Multiple Packages in a Flat Space
abstract: The purpose of this research is to develop a system that shows the loading position of deliveries in a roll cage cart. This study solves the problem of the difficulty of locating individual deliveries in piles. In the proposed system, it is possible to determine the location and size of the package without tearing down the pile of deliveries. The system uses a combination of RFID readers and IMUs to estimate the location of deliveries based on RSSI and azimuth. In addition, the system incorporates the known information of the size of the deliveries and the size of the cart to estimate the position of the delivery in the cart. The proposed algorithm using the constraints of this roll cage cart and the size and coordinates of the packages is used to estimate the location of the packages in the roll cage cart and present it to the delivery workers. This paper reports on the estimation of the positional relationship of multiple packages arrangements in a two-dimensional plane.

articleTitle: Experiments on Taking Loss Methods in Imitation Learning With Bilateral Control
abstract: Recently, motion generation technology using deep learning has been attracting attention as a method for robots to acquire motions adapted to their environment. The combination of imitation learning and bilateral control enables imitation of movements at speeds comparable to those of humans. Previous studies have investigated learning that inputs external information, such as one-hot vectors or image features, but learning to choose actions based on dynamic external information is still being studied. If a camera is used to collect external information, high-level image processing is required, resulting in heavy processing. We thought that the robot's motion generation could cover the problem without high-level image processing. Therefore, this paper examines the task of grasping an object that moves autonomously, independent of the robot, using low-resolution images. We first tried a model that takes loss based on the transformation of angle information into arm hand coordinates, whereas the previous learning model takes loss based on angle information. The results showed that, in imitation learning based on bilateral control, using hand coordinate loss caused a bias in learning the joint angle responses. It also became clear that it is important to learn the joint angle responses with equal weights.

articleTitle: Recognition and Evaluation of Cables for Automated Cutting in Dismantling Process
abstract: Electronic waste (e-waste) continues to increase annually. Automation of the dismantling process is essential for improving recycling rates, but high-mix, low-volume e-wastes make automation particularly challenging, and this leads to reliance on manual operations. The demand for robotic systems that operate without specialized positioning jigs or dismantling lines is increasing. To promote sustainable resource circulation, our aim is to achieve Automation of e-waste dismantling. For this purpose, we propose a novel wire recognition framework and evaluation metrics for wire-cutting tasks. We utilize a pre-trained instance segmentation model fine-tuned with a custom cable image dataset. Because of deformable linear object, cables are harder to recognize than rigid objects and tend to score lower on Average Precision (AP) and Average Recall (AR). Since precise recognition near cutting points is critical for cable-cutting tasks, we propose new evaluation metrics tailored to such operations. Experiments on condenser units demonstrate robust recognition accuracy for cable-cutting, even with overlapping cables. This study validates the effectiveness of the proposed recognition method and evaluation metrics in automating the dismantling process. Future work will address the detection of cutting points and motion generation for cable-cutting operations.

articleTitle: Improvement of Trajectory Estimation Considering Imaging Delay for Autonomous Image Tracking System in Flyby Observation
abstract: In recent years, close approach exploration, called flyby, of asteroids by small spacecraft has attracted attention. In flybys, guidance based on a spacecraft trajectory pre-calculated on the ground is problematic because the accuracy of tracking and imaging is degraded due to uncertainty in geometric parameters during spacecraft navigation. In particular, recent missions tend to fly at higher speeds and shorter proximity distances to the target asteroid. Therefore, the effects of camera measurement error and delay time cannot be ignored, making it difficult to achieve the required performance with simple feedback control. To improve the flyby accuracy, highly accurate trajectory estimation based on measured relative trajectory and the design of a precise control system for the actuator is effective. This paper focuses on accurate trajectory estimation, where a trajectory estimation method based on an online autonomous imaging algorithm is proposed. The least-squares method estimates the relative velocity between the spacecraft and the asteroid. Based on the estimated relative velocity, an accurate target trajectory is generated. In addition, a target trajectory with improved accuracy is generated by correcting the camera's delay time, and the imaging system's actuators are controlled based on the trajectory. The accuracy of the tracking system is evaluated through experiments using an experimental setup that simulates a flyby exploration.

articleTitle: Enhanced Energy Efficiency of Hybrid Reluctance Actuators by Bias Flux Adaptation
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of magnetic bias flux variations on the energy efficiency of hybrid reluctance actuators (HRAs). An analytical model for a variable bias flux HRA is developed to demonstrate the linear relation of the force to current ratio and the bias flux, which is evaluated experimentally by magnetic flux measurements with various permanent magnets. Furthermore, the effects of amplitude and frequency dependencies are analyzed and discussed. To evaluate the energy efficiency, an experimental HRA-based positioning system is dynamically driven and the power consumption is compared for different magnet configurations. The energy efficiency can be improved up to a factor of 3, demonstrating that the bias flux can be used to minimize the energy consumption for a specific operating point.

articleTitle: Control Stiffness-Based Motion Reproduction for Environmental Impedance Variation
abstract: Motion generation technology contributes to the automation of the robots, especially in the industrial field. Imitation learning and motion reproduction system (MRS) are one of the motion generation methods that widely applied. However, machine learning-based methods require a large amount of data and are weak against extrapolation. Although MRS has merit in terms of the data number, it is weak regarding environmental variation. In particular, the environmental impedance variation have occurred, both position and force tracking are impossible. As several conventional studies have been done to reduce only position or force tracking errors, they can not adapt force or position priority tasks, respectively. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel compensation law based on designed control stiffness using the hybrid angle. The validity of this proposal is confirmed by simulation. This paper contributes to the MRS expansion of the environmental impedance variation with consideration of the task's priority physical value.

articleTitle: Teleoperated Orthopedic Drill System Presenting Haptic Information Extended by Bur Tip Position
abstract: In orthopedic surgery, robotic technologies to assist surgeons operating surgical drills to cut bones are being de-veloped, since there is a risk to injure delicate tissues around bones. Penetration detection is useful for surgical drills to enhance safety. However, there is still a risk to damage delicate tissues, even if penetration is detected to stop drills. In this study, a teleoperated haptic drill system implementing a safety enhancement system which extends haptic sensation according to the end effector position is presented. The presented method is composed of the object detection phase and the operator assist phase. In the object detection phase, the position and posture of an object are acquired by the drill system which has the shape model of the object. In the operator assist phase, haptic sensation is extended based on the acquired object information to prevent penetration of the object, while the state of the controller of the drill system is visualized by CG images created by a cutting simulator. The feasibility of the method is confirmed by cutting a pseudo bone.

articleTitle: Sensorless External Force Separation Method for Pedestrian Force Manipulation in Low-Speed Unmanned Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper proposes a method for sensorless separation of external forces acting on low-speed unmanned electric vehicles (EVs) to address a weakness in pedestrian force manipulation, specifically the issue of EVs stopping upon contact with road surface irregularities. This study focuses on suspension resonance transmitted to the wheels, which occurs only during contact with road surface irregularities. In the proposed method, the suspension resonance frequency components of the external forces acting on the wheels are estimated in real time, and their magnitudes are evaluated to achieve external force separation. Experiments were conducted using two types of bumps and two people to confirm that the proposed method enables a low-speed unmanned EV to separate the forces exerted by pedestrians and road surface irregularities, and to stop only when a pedestrian touches the vehicle.

articleTitle: Motion ReTouch: Motion Modification Using Four-Channel Bilateral Control
abstract: Recent research has demonstrated the usefulness of imitation learning in autonomous robot operation. In particular, teaching using four-channel bilateral control, which can obtain position and force information, has been proven effective. However, control performance that can easily execute high-speed, complex tasks in one go has not yet been achieved. We propose a method called Motion ReTouch, which retroactively modifies motion data obtained using four-channel bilateral control. The proposed method enables modification of not only position but also force information. This was achieved by the combination of multilateral control and motion-copying system. The proposed method was verified in experiments with a real robot, and the success rate of the test tube transfer task was improved, demonstrating the possibility of modification force information.

articleTitle: An Optimized Switching Scheme to Reduce the Leakage Current and Power Loss of Transformerless Inverter
abstract: Transformer-less grid-connected inverters gained its popularity in recent times due to their compact design, lower cost, lower weight and overall higher efficiency compared to transformer-based systems. However, among the other issues of the transformer-less solution, leakage current caused by common-mode (CM) voltage fluctuations remains a significant problem, impacting power output, system safety. This paper proposes an optimized switching scheme for a modified H7 transformerless photovoltaic (TLPV) inverter to address the issue by reducing the leakage current and increasing the power quality. Moreover, an optimized unipolar pulse width modulation (UPPWM) strategy is also presented to maintain fairly constant common mode voltage (CMV), effectively suppressing leakage current further. The modified H7 TLPV along with the optimized UPPWM strategy also ensures lower semiconductor power loss and overall better efficiency. The total harmonic distortion (THD) of the grid voltage and current with the optimized pulse width modulation (PWM) strategy found satisfactory which met the standards of IEEE-519. Simulation is conducted in the MATLAB/Simulink environment to validate the performance criteria over the other TLPV structures, feasibility of leakage current reduction and overall power loss. This novel strategy provides an efficient and minimal solution for the next generation TLPV.

articleTitle: Demonstration of an SAC-Based Power Assist System for Pedaling Motions
abstract: This paper considers energy-efficient power assist system for pedaling motions, especially for electric bicycles. Due to the constraints of human musculoskeletal systems, the pedaling motion of bicycles is periodic. Therefore, the velocity of bicycles involve pulsation. In order to improve the energy efficiency of such motion, the suppression of the pulsation is effective. In addition, the variation of power train models of bicycle cannot be ignore when considering assist system to suppress the velocity pulsation. To address this model variation, we propose a SAC (simple adaptive control)-based power assist system. We demonstrate the proposed assist system through an experiment using an electric bicycle.

articleTitle: Motion Generation Utilizing Flexibility for Enhancing Velocity Based on Wave Control
abstract: In recent years, research in the field of robotics has made significant progress, especially in motion control. Mechanisms and control methods that enable robots to perform tasks like humans have been developed. Among these advancements, there has been increasing focus on integrating flexible beams into robotic links. Flexible beams are characterized by high safety due to their flexibility, which also enhances human-robot interaction. However, this flexibility has the potential to cause vibrations. Consequently, many studies have been conducted on vibration suppression techniques, and wave control is one of these approaches. Focusing on human movements, humans can utilize flexibility in tools or body parts effectively, such as golf swings and a throwing motions. Considering a swing motion, the force generated from the torso is transferred to the hands and the golf club, leveraging the flex of the club to increase the ball's travel distance. Based on this concept, this study proposes a control method that utilizes flexibility by controlling the reflected wave through the flexible structure. The proposed method is based on wave control, aiming to increase velocity on the load-side and suppress vibration at the convergence position. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated through experiments.

articleTitle: Safety Critical Control of a Quadrupedal Robot Using MPC-CBF
abstract: Quadrupedal robots have been deployed in numerous challenging environments, such as nuclear facility inspections and industrial surveys. These unstructured and dynamic environments expose the robots to significant safety risks. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel design for a safety-critical control system for quadrupedal robots, integrating Model Predictive Control (MPC) with Control Barrier Functions (CBF) to enhance overall system safety. A comprehensive simulation environment has been established, and results demonstrate that the proposed MPCCBF controller outperforms the conventional MPC controller. Specifically, while the MPC controller alone provides adequate tracking of a desired trajectory in a trot gait, integrating CBF enhances obstacle avoidance and improves stability. This combination allows for navigation through more challenging environments while maintaining accurate trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Vibration Analysis for Dual Three-phase PMSM under Single Three-phase Conditions
abstract: For dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors (DTP-PMSMs), the single three-phase (STP) operating mode is the simpler and quicker fault-tolerant operation mode, commonly applied in the presence of single, two, or three phases open-circuit faults in the windings. In this paper, the electromagnetic vibration response, electromagnetic output performance and torque ripple are compared for two STP conditions in order to determine the suitable scenarios for each condition to achieve better vibration behavior and output performance under open-circuit faults. Firstly, a rational design of the DTP-PMSM system is given. Secondly, the distribution and amplitude of the harmonics of armature magnetomotive force (MMF), radial and tangential air-gap electromagnetic force density (AEFD) under different operating conditions are analyzed. The vibration response and electromagnetic torque are also compared. The results indicate that electromagnetic vibrations under the STP condition are more severe, especially under Condition II. Under open-circuit faults, Condition I is applicable to scenarios with higher vibration requirements, while Condition II is applicable to scenarios with higher electromagnetic output performance requirements. if the motor vibration level index is satisfied. Finally, the modal and vibration test are conducted under the DTP condition. The simulation results are in good agreement with the test results, validating the effectiveness of the structural finite element analysis model and vibration prediction method.

Author Keywords: Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Proposal of an Analysis Method Using the Nonsmooth DEM Approach for Space Membrane Deployment Structures with Experimental Validation
abstract: Membrane deployment structures are used in spacecrafts due to their lightweight nature and high stowage efficiency. Currently, numerous analytical methods have been proposed to model the behavior of such flexible structures. However, the complex dynamics of membrane deployment in space lead to high computational loads in conventional analysis methods. Thus, there is a need to develop a low-cost, computationally efficient method that can accurately reproduce membrane deployment dynamics. This study proposes an analytical approach applying the Nonsmooth DEM to analyze membrane motion modeled by particle systems, aiming to reduce computational cost. To evaluate this method, both simulation and ground-based experiment were conducted using a mesh structure that simulates flexible membrane. Comparison of experimental and simulation results indicated that the proposed method was validated as an approach for analyzing membrane deployment structures.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Short Distance Landing Control with Reverse Thrust of Variable Pitch Propeller for Fixed Wing Electric Aircraft
abstract: In the aviation industry, a short landing distance for aircraft is quite important which may broaden the usage of it. For a propeller-driven aircraft, variable pitch propeller (VPP) is widely used to create reverse thrust as air brake. However, because of the complexity of VPP mechanism and low controllability of internal combustion engine, a hydraulic type VPP may not allow a large range variation of the pitch angle. On the other hand, regarding electric aircrafts, its controllability is approximately 100 times higher than conventional engine thanks to a fast response of electric motor. This characteristic may make it possible to use wider range of pitch angle to make larger thrust for shorter landing distance than usual. In this paper, a basic study of the feasibility of using VPP to achieve the short landing distance control for a fixed wing electric aircraft is conducted. A pitch angle transition for opposite direction as to a conventional transition is proposed for the larger reverse thrust. An experiment is conducted to obtain a static characteristic of VPP for the larger thrust. To the end, simulations are conducted to verify the proposed pitch angle transition for shorter landing distance with parameter identified in experiments, and it is confirmed that the proposed method can reduce the landing distance up to 30 % compared to the conventional pitch transition.

articleTitle: CTPU Based MetaMetarial Behaviour as a Soft Strain Sensor
abstract: The surge in flexible and wearable electronics, fueled by advancements in smart technologies and growing market demand, has highlighted the importance of auxetic sensors for applications in healthcare, medical rehabilitation, soft robotics, and human-machine interfaces. For widespread adoption, these sensors must offer high sensitivity, substantial stretchability, and long-term durability. This study explores the possibilities of realizing such wearable soft sensors based on conductive thermoplastic polyurethane (cTPU) 3D printing enhanced with auxetic mechanical metamaterials. Following simultaneous empirical mechanical and electrical measurements, auxetic soft sensor designs were compared with numerical simulations. Results suggest that such soft sensors based on metamaterials are great candidates for applications in healthcare and robotics when realized with 3D printing.

articleTitle: A Remote Control Method for Transport Two-Wheeled Mobile Robot
abstract: This paper investigates the deployment of transport Two-Wheeled Mobile Robots (TWMRs) within warehouse environments. TWMRs have superior maneuverability and a smaller footprint compared to conventional steering-type Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs). This feature makes TWMRs well-suited for narrow spaces and high-reach tasks. Despite these advantages, TWMRs are inherently unstable, necessitating sophisticated control systems to maintain balance. In this study, we propose a control system that enables remote operation of the TWMR, allowing the operator to adjust the pitch angle command. The TWMR is equipped with various control mechanisms, including Disturbance Observer (DOB), PD controller and Lyapunov controller. These components work in conjunction to stabilize the TWMR and enhance the translational position tracking performance. Simulation results demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach, showing that the proposed system successfully stabilized the TWMR and reduced pitch angle variations, especially under load conditions. It also suggested the potential of integrating human control ability with advanced control systems for improved TWMR performance.

articleTitle: Investigation Into Suitable Number of Stator Slots of MW Class SPMSM Considering Laminated Rotor in Hybrid Propulsion System of Aircraft
abstract: This paper investigates the number of stator slots of a MW class surface permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) in the hybrid propulsion system of an aircraft for enhancing efficiency when its rotor is axially laminated. The MW class SPMSM needs to achieve high output power density and efficiency simultaneously. In general, as the output power of electrical motor increases, heat generation becomes a serious problem. Hence, this paper comprehensively evaluates suitable number of stator slots in the MW class SPMSM considering laminated permanent magnets and retainer rings using three-dimensional finite element analysis (3D-FEA) to reduce the total loss.

articleTitle: Study of Frictional and Impact Transients in Active-Passive Mechanical Pair
abstract: We consider an active-passive mechanical pair in which the relative motion of the latter is constrained by the mechanical impact. The system dynamics is described by two previously introduced modeling frameworks of force transition and dissipation through the nonlinear Coulomb friction and structural damping, the latter in accord with Hertzian contact theory. The focus of the recent study is on combining both interaction mechanisms and on a detailed experimental evaluation which discloses validity of the modeling assumptions. Such mechanical pair interactions can be found in various mechatronic systems and mechanisms, like for example clutches, backlash elements, sliding items on the shaking and tilting tables, conveyor belts and others. This practical study demonstrates and discusses the transients of a vibro-impact dynamics and shows the theoretical developments in line with experimental results.

articleTitle: Instantaneous Voltage Regulation-based Sliding Mode Direct Torsion Torque Control for High-Backforward-Drivability Actuation
abstract: This paper proposes a high-response torque control method for a surface permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) with reduction gearing for interactive operation. In robots performing interactive tasks, backforward-drivability of the geared SPMSM is important. The backforward-drivability is defined as the ease of manipulating the load-side of the geared motor by external forces. Torsion torque control has been proposed to enhance this drivability. However, conventional torsion torque control is limited in response speed due to the high system order and reliance on a minor loop current controller. In this study, we propose a high-response sliding mode direct torsion torque control for the geared SPMSM modeled as a two-inertia resonant system. The proposed method achieves rapid response by eliminating the current controller and controlling inverter switches directly. Numerical simulations and experiments confirm that the proposed method provides high-response torsion torque control.

articleTitle: Design of A Novel Statically Balanced Mechanism for End-effector-type Upper Limb Assistance
abstract: Partial loss of upper limb motor function is a typical sequela of stroke. To help such patients actively cope with daily challenges and improve their quality of life, limb functional assistances play important roles. To this end, this paper proposes a three-degree-of-freedom parallel mechanism, which can be used for human upper limb assistance. The base of the proposed mechanism is a circular track that can be attached to the waist of the human body. The mechanism consists of two chains containing parallelogram linkage, which presents good constraints for the mobile platform and facilitates the static balance design by adding springs, thereby providing reliable assistive functions and lightweight portability. The mobility of the proposed mechanism is analyzed via the screw theory, and it is verified that the mechanism generates the aimed movements. Then, the kinematic analysis of the mechanism is presented. Finally, the static balance design is carried out in detail, and the spring constants of the three added springs are calculated. The result shows that the mechanism can achieve perfect static balance. The proposed mechanism is expected to provide a potential candidate for assistive devices and be developed into a prototype providing upper limb assistance.

articleTitle: Human-Coordinated Control of Two-Wheeled Robot with Elastic Handle
abstract: The electronic commerce (EC) market in the BtoC industry has grown rapidly in recent years. Consequently, the volume of parcel delivery services is also rising, and the physical burden on the delivery staff is increasing. Therefore, this study aims to develop a new transport support system that enhances operability and followability. In this method, an elastic handle is attached to a two-wheeled robot. The elastic handle reduces the turning radius, improves the tracking performance, and minimizes operational discomfort as it deforms to follow the direction the user pulls. However, the elasticity of the handle may cause the robot's pitch angle to tilt excessively, or the handle may vibrate owing to elasticity, leading to reduced operability. This study implements stabilization control in the translational and pitch angle directions to address these issues, considering disturbances and using a Lyapunov controller. In the turning direction, turning angle control is implemented using load-side acceleration control with the handle side as the load. The effects of the elastic handle and control system were verified through simulations. Verification results confirmed that the system can follow human operations and reduce human effort while stabilizing the robot body.

articleTitle: High-Performance Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensor based on Multi-Walled CNT for Motion Detection
abstract: High-performance flexible sensors characterized by high sensitivity, low detection limits, a wide working pressure range, and rapid response times have gained significant attention recently due to their essential role in advancing wearable smart devices, human-machine interaction, and healthcare systems. In this work, we present the fabrication of highly flexible and sensitive capacitive pressure sensors using Multi-Walled Carbon Nanotube (MWCNT)/Ecoflex composite electrodes. The sensors were fabricated using a straightforward dipping-drying method, facilitating the uniform adhesion of CNTs to the elastomer matrix. The resulting pressure sensors demonstrate exceptional performance, exhibiting high sensitivity (2.2% kPa⁻¹), fast response time (< 40 ms), and an extensive working range (0.03-30 kPa), with strong linearity (r² = 0.983). Several applications of human machine interaction are successfully demonstrated by using the developed sensors. This work presents a cost-effective and simple way to fabricate flexible pressure sensors for use as wearable devices across a range of applications, including motion monitoring, hand gesture detection, and human-machine interfaces (HMIs).

articleTitle: Drive Stabilization of Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Maglev Planar Motor Based on Closed Loop System Identification
abstract: Magnetic levitation planar motor can move at high speed and with high accuracy, and prevent vibration and noise because of no friction. This technology leads to the application of a transport system that requires high-speed and high-precision movement. However, the design of appropriate control algorithms is essential to achieve stability and high-speed, high-precision control of the maglev planar motor. In this research, we stabilized a maglev planar motor on the basis of system identification. Initially, we designed a whole control system for the movement of the maglev planar motor. Furthermore, we conducted system identification and verified that the maglev planar motor works with the designed control system and evaluated its motion performance. Through experiments, it was confirmed that accurate motion control was possible. This research is expected to be a basis for improving control performance soon.

articleTitle: Monitoring of Food Fouling in A Plate Heat Exchanger Using Heat Flux Sensor
abstract: This article aims to describe the effect of fluid flow rate on soymilk fouling in a flat plate heat exchanger at a surface temperature of 95 °C using a foil heat flux sensor. The experiment was conducted in the pilot-scale fouling test rig for 6 hours each run. Five product flow rates of 1.5, 3.0, 4.5, 6.0, and 7.5 1/min were studied. The results showed that a heat flux sensor could be used to real-time monitor the changes of soymilk fouling deposits formed on the heated surface. Fouling curves of soymilk at flow rates of 3.0 and 4.5 1/min exhibited a falling rate pattern, while at flow rate of 1.5 showed an asymptotic pattern. It was found that the thickness of fouling decreased with increasing product flow rate in the range of 1.5 - 4.5 1/min. At higher flow rates, only a slightly thin film of fouling layer was observed.

articleTitle: A Torque-Sensor-Based Nonlinear Observer for Shockless Torque Control of Two-Inertia Systems with Backlash
abstract: Two-inertia resonant systems are used to represent several motion control systems with resonance modes such as drivetrains and robot joints, offering a more flexible approach for their control compared to single-inertia representations. Controlling the transmitted torsion torque (also known as joint torque) to the load allows to effectively control the driven load of the system regardless of the resonant mode, which can be done by employing torque sensors. However, many real systems contain some degree of joint backlash, which causes a large, impulse-like shock on torque reversals due to the mechanical play of the joint elements, which can lead to undesired behavior and even destruction of the mechanical elements of the system being controlled. While torque sensors are able to sense whether the drive and load-sides are in contact or not, they don't give information on the relative angle between both sides, which is necessary for achieving shockless torque control. This paper introduces a novel nonlinear observer structure based on torque sensing that is able to estimate all the load-side states even when backlash occurs. This new observer is then implemented in a torsion torque control scheme that employs model predictive control during backlash gap traversings to achieve shockless control. Simulation results confirm the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Nano-Acoustic Subsurface Imaging for Atomic Force Microscopy
abstract: The feasibility of a new imaging regime for sub-surface Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) is investigated using synthetic aperture focusing technique. This technique uses two Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) probes to emit acoustic pulses and sense echoes. Unlike other existing subsurface AFM methods, Nano-Acoustic Subsurface AFM (NASAFM) provides cross-sectional images of a sample below the surface with depth information in the nanometre scale. In order to determine the best resolution, two ideal wideband AFM probes are considered in simulation. The results show that a 20 ps pulse with a bandwidth of 330 GHz was able to resolve two 50 nm discs, 500 nm below the surface, separated by 340 nm. Future work is needed to understand the relation between resolution and bandwidth, the optimal imaging parameters, and the sensing technique.

articleTitle: Real-Time Tuning of Transformation Matrices for Decoupling Control in Dual-Drive Stage Systems Using Gaussian Process
abstract: High-precision gantry stages are crucial in industrial equipment for fine processing. Achieving high-speed, accurate positioning is essential for improved throughput and product quality, particularly for large stages where low resonant modes and changes in transfer characteristics during operation present challenges. This paper introduces a method for real-time adjustment of transformation matrices for decoupling based on pre-acquired frequency response data and Gaussian process regression. The proposed approach allows for the implementation of adaptive, real-time control adjustments and pre-computed stability checks. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through experiments conducted with an XY gantry stage.

articleTitle: Investigation of Relationship between Electrode Integration Method and Force-to-Volume Ratio in Force Generation System Using Corona Discharge
abstract: A force generation mechanism utilizing corona discharge has the advantages of being lightweight, compact, and having no moving parts. The general structure of an electrode used to generate corona discharge is a wire on the high-voltage side and a flat plate on the ground side. To gain greater force generated by corona discharge, it is necessary to install and integrate a large number of electrodes. However, if a large number of electrodes are integrated, the required volume will increase. Therefore, a method of integrating the electrodes to increase the force-to-volume ratio is needed. Therefore, this paper comprehensively examines the two-dimensional arrangement of electrodes on the ground side and investigates the relationship with the force-to-volume ratio. Specifically, the force-to-volume ratio was investigated when the ground side was made of hollow hexagons, squares, or triangles compared to the wire-plate electrode. Also, since it is known that the force is more significant when needles are used on the high-voltage side rather than wires, the high-voltage side was made into a needle for electrodes with hollow polygons. The experimental results show that the force-to-volume ratios of the needle-hollow polygon electrodes were larger when the applied voltage was low, around 20 kV, and that of the wire-plate electrode was larger when the applied voltage was higher than 30 kV. These results show the relationship between the method of integrating the electrodes and the force-to-volume ratio, which was unknown in corona discharge. They can be used as a reference in the design of actuators.

articleTitle: Horn-Muller-von der Wense Gearbox: A Novel Approach to Uninterrupted Torque Transmission During Gear Changes (HMW-Gear)
abstract: The Horn-Muller-von der Wense Gear (HMW-Gear) is a newly developed transmission system that is capable of transmitting uninterrupted torque during the switching process and was developed and manufactured over a three-year period. The project began with a purely mathematical approach, wherein various functions were analyzed to address the question of how to change gears without interrupting torque. Significant efforts were made to develop special cogwheels based on this approach. An additional test bench was constructed. In addition to a fun-damental explanation of the invention and detailed information on its implementation, initial validation measurement results are presented in this publication. The HMW -Gear switching principle is protected under the European Patent Law [4].

articleTitle: Anti-Slip Power-Assist Control System for Electric Transporter Based on Slip Acceleration Control
abstract: Electric transporters are capable of realizing comfortable cargo transportation by sensing the pushing force applied by the operator and amplifying it through the driving wheels, greatly reducing workload on tasks such as in fruit harvesting in narrow environments or transportation of supplies during environmental disasters, where regular vehicles are not able to access. However, on conditions such as sandy or muddy roads the driving wheels slip, causing the operator to momentarily lose control of the transporter. In this research, we propose a power-assist control method with integrated slip supression through slip acceleration control, which is easily achieved by wheel and vehicle body acceleration measurements. Through experimental verification we confirmed that our proposed method greatly improve assisting performance even in slippery conditions.

articleTitle: Automatic Emoticons Insertion System Based on Acoustic Information of User Voice: 4th Report on Silence Removal for Generalized Emotion Estimation and Improved Visual Representations
abstract: This study proposes an automatic emoticon insertion system based on acoustic information from user voice. The system estimates emotions from acoustic features using Support Vector Machine (SVM) and inserts corresponding emoticons to enhance emotional communication in text-based social media. Key advancements include the removal of silent segments from training model voice data, improving emotion estimation accuracy and generalizability, as well as a refined visual representation method to address the polysemous nature of emoticons. Experimental results show a significant performance improvement, with accuracy rising to 75.12% compared to the previous model. These findings lay the groundwork for real-time applications, supporting enhanced user communication efficiency and emotion expressiveness in digital contexts.

articleTitle: Fast Position Control of a Large Radio Telescope's Secondary Mirror Using Iterative Learning
abstract: In this paper, we address a complex motion control problem of fast and precise positioning of the secondary mirror in a large radio telescope, which exhibits strong nonlinear behavior and is greatly influenced by gravity and wind. We optimally integrate cascade feedback control, kinematic feedforwards, and iterative learning control to achieve the required positioning accuracy in minimum time. The kinematic feedforwards are generated by a modified online jerk-limited trajectory generator with high numerical accuracy. This novel triple combination marks a first in telescopes motion control, yielding exceptional positioning performance as confirmed by experimental results.

articleTitle: A Sequential Hermaphrodite Coupling Mechanism for Lattice-based Modular Robots
abstract: Lattice-based modular robot systems have been envisioned for large-scale construction in extreme environments, such as space. To optimize system weight and power consumption, heterogeneous approaches combining active and passive coupling interfaces have been explored. Coupling mechanisms for heterogeneous structural modules must satisfy challenging requirements: maintaining flat surfaces when uncoupled, enabling single-sided coupling and decoupling, and compatibility with passive interfaces. We propose a novel mechanical coupling mechanism that addresses these challenges by actively transitioning between male and female states. The design integrates multiple practical features: 90° rotational symmetry, electrical pathways for communication and power supply, and mechanical hooks that maintain secure connections even without power. Experimental validation demonstrated the reliability and practicality of the mechanism, confirming its tolerance to misalignment, the sufficient load capacity, and effectiveness of its current-based failsafe system. This coupling mechanism represents the first solution to simultaneously achieve these capabilities, enabling efficient and reliable reconfiguration of heterogeneous modular robotic systems.

articleTitle: Anomaly Cause Classification in the Extrusion Process Using Prompt-Based Segmentation and Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: In this study, a method was developed to detect anomalies caused by incorrect process condition settings in the extrusion process for catheter tube manufacturing and to classify the causes of these anomalies. The proposed method first employs a prompt-based segmentation technique to segment the extruded resin, and then extracts the time history of the area and height ratio of the segmented resin to classify the cause of the anomaly. A specially developed deep learning network is designed to use the signal in the time domain to classify the cause of the anomaly, while also visualizing and analyzing the reasoning in the frequency domain. This network performs feature extraction on the time history of the height ratio and area, using a softsign function and power pooling to preserve frequency domain information as much as possible, thus enabling visualization of the basis for determining the cause of the anomaly. We collected a total of 47 minutes and 53 seconds of data under 14 process conditions and organized it into seven classes for analysis. The proposed method achieved 100% classification accuracy using data obtained under the given process conditions, demonstrating nearly perfect results.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Velocity Estimation Method Using Chebyshev Expansion
abstract: In motion control, velocity is required to be estimated with less delay and less error, but the two are trade-offs because of an encoder's quantization noise, and they are difficult to make both small simultaneously. This paper aims to overcome the trade-off when conventional methods are used. This paper proposes an FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) implementation method for a model-free velocity estimation using Chebyshev expansion. The use of Chebyshev expansion enables better rejection of quantization noise from the measured data than using a frequency-domain filter. The estimation method is realized by a single inner product calculation, which takes 3μs of computation time on FPGA. The performance of the proposed method is validated by a velocity estimation from actual encoder data.

articleTitle: Generalized Dynamics of Non-Grounded Systems with Series Elastic Actuators and Effect of Actuator Base Fixation on Force Control Robustness
abstract: This paper proposes a generalized dynamics model for a Non-Grounded System (NGS) mounted with a Reaction Force Sensing Series Elastic Actuator (RFSEA), focusing on scenarios where the actuator's base is unfixed and interacts with the ground. In RFSEA-based force control, the actuator base, which provides the necessary reaction force as dictated by Newton's third law, plays a critical role. This study examines how the interaction between the actuator base and the ground it is attached to influences the response of the series elasticity that generates force in the RFSEA. The investigation involves two steps. First, a generalized dynamics model that considers the dynamics between the actuator base and the ground is derived. Second, the Small Gain Theorem (SGT) is applied to evaluate the robustness of force control under load-side model uncertainties when a Force-based Disturbance Observer (FDOB), originally designed for GS, is adapted to NGS. The analysis reveals that force control utilizing FDOB can become unstable when the actuator base is unfixed, and simulations validate these findings.

articleTitle: Quick Response Valve for Active Control of Pneumatic Vibration Isolation Tables
abstract: Active control of pneumatic vibration isolation tables requires extreme preciseness, due to the rapid growth of the demand for well performing precision positioning stages. And in order to meet this need, this paper proposes a new type of pneumatic valve for the control of air flow rates supplied into the air spring of the vibration isolator. Valves in general, have certain nonlinearities which degrade the precision of the control of air flow rates. Since the air flow rates are mainly dependent of the poppet position, the new valve equips an internal position sensor. Using this sensor, a poppet position inner feedback (FB) control, as well as a model based feedforward (FF) control is introduced in the control system. This method compensates for the air disturbance force to the poppet position and allows fast control of the pressure inside the air spring. The effectiveness of the proposed system is demonstrated through pressure tracking experiments.

articleTitle: Climbing Motion Generation for Humanoid Agents through Deep Reinforcement Learning with Optimization Constraints
abstract: By enabling a humanoid to perform human-like movements, it can be utilized in various applications, such as assisting humans and motion analysis. While research on tasks like walking and transporting objects with humanoids has advanced, studies involving climbing walls remain underexplored. In climbing, while the movement of the hands gripping the wall is crucial, whole-body movement is also essential for reducing the load on the hands. This study focuses on bouldering as an example where full-body coordination is critical during climbing, and employs deep reinforcement learning to train a humanoid in a simulation environment to climb while minimizing hand load. As a result, the humanoid achieved a high success rate in the given task, demonstrating that deep reinforcement learning can successfully teach climbing methods that alleviate the load on the hands. Furthermore, the study suggests that gradually increasing the weight assigned to a subtask is an effective strategy when simultaneously learning two tasks.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Coefficient of Performance in Heat Pump Systems and its Application to Climate Intervention
abstract: This study presents an optimization of the parameters of a heat pump system that maximizes the Coefficient of Performance (COP) while ensuring the required flow rate and temperature variations in a constrained power and space environment. We modeled the refrigerant cycle of the heat pump cooling system using the numerical analysis software MATLAB/SimulinklSimscape, and employed the Nelder-Mead method to maximize the COP under constant cooling power conditions. The optimization process successfully increased COP by a factor of 1.3 without compromising cooling capacity. Additionally, we conducted a cooling simulation with a weather simulator, the Weather Research and Forecasting Model (WRF), to verify the reduction in the typhoon's central pressure.

articleTitle: Problems and Design for a Cable-Driven Device for Elbow-Wrist Assistance
abstract: This paper presents the design of a portable, lightweight, cable-driven exoskeleton for upper limb rehabilitation and exercise. Based on a parallel mechanism driven by cables, the device is designed to assist with simultaneous motion of elbow and wrist during exercise and rehabilitation. It adapts to each patient's specific needs and, thanks to its portability, is intended for autonomous use at home. An analysis of the challenges and requirements in developing such assisting devices is discussed, and lab experiences from previous designs support the effectiveness of the proposed solution for limb motion assistance.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Driving Force Control for EVs Using Road Condition Estimation with Machine Learning Image Recognition and Vehicle Dynamics
abstract: Driving Force Control (DFC) for in-wheel motor electric vehicles has been studied for years. To realize DFC, setting the slip ratio limiter (SRL) through appropriate estimation of the road-tire model is essential on low friction surface. However setting the slip ratio limiter based on vehicle dynamics has faced the issue of tire model estimation delay, a fixed SRL has been commonly used in the traditional DFC. This paper proposes a method to quickly adapt to changes in road conditions by the fusion of vision based SRL estimation with vehicle dynamics based SRL estimation. At the moment of road surface condition transition, the vision-based estimation is referenced to compensate for the delay in the dynamics-based approach using fusion algorithm. Experiments and simulations confirmed an increase in traction force on low friction roads through appropriate setting of slip ratio limiter. Experimental results demonstrated that immediately after a sudden change of road surface condition, the proposed method increased driving force by 15 % compared to conventional DFC systems with a variable SRL based solely on dynamics-based estimation.

articleTitle: Variable-Frequency Imitation Learning for Variable-Speed Motion
abstract: Conventional methods of imitation learning for variable-speed motion have difficulty extrapolating speeds because they rely on learning models running at a constant sampling frequency. This study proposes variable-frequency imitation learning (VFIL), a novel method for imitation learning with learning models trained to run at variable sampling frequencies along with the desired speeds of motion. The experimental results showed that the proposed method improved the velocity-wise accuracy along both the interpolated and extrapolated frequency labels, in addition to a 12.5 % increase in the overall success rate.

articleTitle: Improved Accuracy of Rotor Position Estimation in PMSM Deadbeat Predictive Control Using ADALINE Network-Based Filter
abstract: This paper proposes a highly accurate rotor position estimation method based on deadbeat predictive control and sensorless control using current derivative values. Compared with PI control, deadbeat predictive control offers better dynamic performance but is more susceptible to harmonics. In this study, the rotor position estimation accuracy was improved by adaptively estimating and removing harmonic components superimposed on the current using ADALINE network-based filter. The simulation results showed that the proposed method reduced the number of rotor position estimation errors, and favorable results were obtained under varying velocities and sudden load fluctuations.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Tilt-Wing eVTOL Using Aerodynamic Coupling Observer and Wing Angle Correction Method
abstract: Recently, electric vertical take-off and landing has been attracting attention as a potential solution for alleviation of urban traffic congestion, alternative tools of delivery, and inspection missions in disaster situations. We focus on the advantages of the tilt-wing type, such as the low drag of the wing during ascent and the ability to use the propeller wake even during transition phase to control the lift by flap. This paper focuses on the how to determine the tilt angle reference to track the desired trajectory. Some previous research uses the tilt angle that achieve trim state as the reference. It has a disadvantage that the actuator in the inner layer saturates when the high acceleration command is given or when wind disturbance exists. Proposed wing angle correction method enables aircraft to track the trajectory even in those situations by correcting the tilt angle to solve a optimization problem that considers the actuator input and disturbance estimated by the inner layer DOB. The results of the numerical simulation and hardware in the loop simulation show that the proposed control system reduces the actuator saturation and improves the trajectory tracking performance.

articleTitle: Research on Extraction and Reproduction of Human Calligraphy Motion Using Motion Sensor and 6-axis Force Sensor
abstract: In recent years, robot systems to reproduce human motions such as a motion-copying system have been studied in the industrial field. The motion-copying system uses bilateral control to extract human motions. However, the robot's mechanics may affect human operability. This paper proposes the human motion extraction system using a motion sensor and a force sensor. The proposed system does not interfere with human operation. This study focuses on human calligraphy motions as the dexterous human motions. The extraction system extracts the brush position data from a motion sensor. In addition, the system extracts the force data applied to the brush from a force sensor. By using the extracted position and force data, a parallel robot reproduces human calligraphy motions. The reproducibility of the skills and the effectiveness of this system were confirmed by comparing the original characters with the reproduced characters.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Inverse Control of Pneumatic Soft Robotic Actuators with On-Off Valves: Simulated Performance
abstract: This article describes a data-driven control method for fast and accurate pressure regulation of pneumatic soft robotic actuators with on-off valves. Due to the non-linearity and binary control input, linear controllers are not ideal for pressure regulation as they must be tuned conservatively, which results in a slow transient response. Alternatively, non-linear methods can provide a faster response time but are complicated by the need for an accurate model. This article proposes an inverse control approach, where the control action is parameterized by the valve on-time, and the system output is the cumulative change in pressure after the control action is complete and all system transients have decayed. This approach eliminates the need for a dynamic model and results in a small space of input-output combinations that can be measured from a calibration experiment. The result is a non-linear inverse controller that does not require a dynamic model. The proposed method is compared in simulation to a hysteresis controller with three different valve orifice diameters. Significant improvements to the pressure regulation and valve lifetime are observed. This method is expected to find applications in soft robotics where fast step changes and dynamic trajectories are required.

articleTitle: Low-Computational-Cost Edge-Computing Robot System for Fruit Automatic Harvesting Using a Raspberry Pi
abstract: In recent decades, the agricultural labor force in developed countries has steadily declined, leading to severe shortages of workers. To address this problem, automating various agricultural tasks has become increasingly urgent. This paper focuses specifically on the robotic automation of fruit harvesting. Existing automated harvesting robot systems have several limitations: They lack flexibility as they target only specific fruits, require large batteries because of high power consumption, which reduces operating times, and incur high costs. To reduce power consumption and overall costs, the proposed system uses a single RGB-D sensor and a Raspberry Pi as its sole computational resource. To ensure flexibility, the system utilizes shared peduncle characteristics among different fruits. After identifying the fruit to be harvested, the system locates the connecting peduncle and determines the target cutting pose. The experimental results indicated an average success rate of 91% and an average time of 12.7 seconds to harvest each fruit.

articleTitle: Consideration of Micro-Macro 4-channel Bilateral Control Scheme Using Piezoelectric Actuator
abstract: In micro-manipulations such as cell manipulation, if the operator can feel the tactile sensation of the object, those operations are expected to be more efficient. Scale bilateral control, in which micro-manipulation is performed remotely and position and force information is transmitted bidirectionally between the two systems, could be one of the solutions for tactile transmission. In this control, the use of a linear motor as a human-operating system and a stacked piezoelectric actuator as a micro-manipulating system has been proposed. In this context, a linear motor is an inertial system, and a piezoelectric actuator is a stiff system. However, the control scheme and theory of bilateral control have been established only for inertial systems. In previous studies, piezoelectric actuators were modeled as inertial systems, and the construction of bilateral control systems according to the scheme of inertial systems was attempted. This paper attempts to construct bilateral control by modeling piezoelectric actuators as a second-order linear system close to the actuator's physical properties. Experiments revealed that the proposed bilateral control scheme performs well as the conventional scheme. This study contributes to constructing bilateral control between two systems with different structures.

articleTitle: A Novel Sensor Design of Angle Measurement for Harsh Environments
abstract: This paper presents a novel angle measurement sensor designed for operation in harsh environments. Typically, angle measurement is performed using encoders that are directly attached to motors, actuators, or both, depending on the application. These encoders can be either incremental or absolute and may utilize various sensing principles, such as optical, magnetic, or resistive methods. However, most conventional sensors exhibit significant limitations when deployed in extreme conditions, such as radioactive environments, high temperatures, or high moisture levels. In such scenarios, robotic systems often experience failures due to sensor malfunctions, making the development of robust angle measurement solutions essential for ensuring fail-safe operation. This paper introduces a novel angle measurement sensor based on the variation of electromagnetic inductance, specifically designed for use in harsh environments. Experimental results obtained from a laboratory setup validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A DYC system for 4WID Electric Vehicles via Fuzzy-Nonsingular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a novel Direct Yaw Moment Control (DYC) system designed to bolster the stability of four-wheel independent drive (4WID) electric vehicles in diverse extreme driving conditions. Our proposed system is developed based on the design of Non-singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control (NFTSMC) methods to calculate two optimal additional yaw moments, each targeting specific control objectives: the desired yaw rate and the desired sideslip angle. These calculated values are then intelligently weighted in real time using a Fuzzy Logic system to determine the final additional yaw moment applied to the vehicle. The stability of the NFTSMC methods is rigorously ensured through the Lyapunov theory. Simulation results underscore the efficacy of our proposed DYC system, particularly in navigating through extreme driving scenarios. Comparisons with no control and fixed weight-based SMC strategies demonstrated significant improvements in both yaw rate and sideslip angle tracking performance. The proposed method not only amplifies control effectiveness, ensuring swift convergence and high precision, but also substantially mitigates chattering phenomena, as evidenced by yaw moment and torque observations.

articleTitle: Preliminary Investigation of Spring-Based Gravity Compensation for an Upper Limb Assistive Robot
abstract: Upper limb assistive robots have been widely developed due to their ability to aid user movement and reduce caregiver workload. In our previous work, we introduced a wearable end-effector-type upper limb assistive robot, WELiBot. To enhance the robot's portability and reduce the required actuation torque, this work investigates gravity compensation for WELiBot's mechanism using springs. Following the 1-DOF gravity compensation principle, springs were designed for lifting and reaching movement respectively. The effectiveness of this compensation effect was then evaluated by comparing the necessary torque at the actuating joints with and without springs. This work offers insight into gravity compensation for parallel mechanisms and contributes to the future development of WELiBot.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Multiple Resonant Filter Design Integrating Notch Filters and Peak Filters in Dual-Stage Actuator Hard Disk Drives
abstract: Magnetic-head positioning performance of hard disk drives in data center infrastructures is fundamental to the large storage capacity. The aim of this paper is to develop a feedback controller design method for hard disk drives integrating robust stabilization and disturbance rejection simultaneously. Notch filters for resonant mode stabilization and peak filters for disturbance rejection are designed simultaneously by resonant filters in the same structure. Multiple resonant filters are designed by frequency response data-driven iterative convex optimization for robust stabilization and disturbance rejection at the same time. The disturbance rejection performance improvement with robust stability is validated in a dual-stage actuator hard disk drive benchmark problem.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Nano Electrical Resistive Tomography for Subsurface Atomic Force Microscopy
abstract: This article investigates the feasibility of using a dual-cantilever atomic force microscope for imaging the electrical properties of a sample below the surface. Principles from macro-scale electrical resistive tomography are adapted to utilize measurements from a dual-probe atomic force microscope. A deep-learning method is employed to perform the inversion process and construct the tomography. Simulation results demonstrate that electrical resistive tomography is possible at the nanometre scale but improvements to the inversion algorithms are needed before moving to experimental applications.

articleTitle: Error-Feedback Model for Output Correction in Bilateral Control-Based Imitation Learning
abstract: In recent years, imitation learning using neural networks has enabled robots to perform flexible tasks. However, since neural networks operate in a feedforward structure, they do not possess a mechanism to compensate for output errors. To address this limitation, we developed a feedback mechanism to correct these errors. By employing a hierarchical structure for neural networks comprising lower and upper layers, the lower layer was controlled to follow the upper layer. Additionally, using a multi-layer perceptron in the lower layer, which lacks an internal state, enhanced the error feedback. In the character-writing task, this model demonstrated improved accuracy in writing previously untrained characters. In the character-writing task, this model demonstrated improved accuracy in writing previously untrained characters. Through autonomous control with error feedback, we confirmed that the lower layer could effectively track the output of the upper layer. This study represents a promising step toward integrating neural networks with control theories.

articleTitle: Vibration and Noise Optimization of Surfaced Mounted PMSM used in EMP
abstract: Take advantages of the high power density, fast response, heavy load capacity, Electrical Motor Pump (EMP) has been widely used in airplane, ships, and mineral equipment. For some special applications, extreme low vibration and noise are required. The surfaced mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (SPMSM) has low torque ripples, thus it also has low vibration and noise. However, it is still far from the extreme requirements.
